full_judgment:
D.C. Bhattacharya, J.—This appeal by special leave is against a judgment of a Division Bench of the Dacca High Court in a Second Appeal, setting aside an appellate judgment of reversal and dismissing a suit brought by the appellant for declaration of title and recovery of possession. 

 17. It is to be pointed out that the learned Judges of the High Court appear to have not kept in view the limitation of the jurisdiction of the said Court in dealing with a second appeal. As has been noticed above, they can interfere with a finding of fact only if it is warranted under the provision of section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, that is, only on the ground of an error of law or a substantial error or defect in the procedure. It is found that a particular finding of the last Court of fact has been vitiated by any such error the same may be set aside, and in that circumstance the case is generally sent back to the said Court for a rehearing of the matter on evidence by the same Court. The High Court may, however, hear the case on evidence in exercise of its power under section 103 C.P. Code if it so chooses. But in the said event, it shall have go to into evidence fully and adequately just like a court of fact and come to its own findings on a proper assessment of the evidence op record. Even if the decision of the learned Judges of the High Court taking the view that the judgment of the Court of appeal below was not a proper judgment of reversal was correct, they could not have rest contented by merely setting aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court and restoring the Judgment of the .trial court. There should have been in that event a fresh decision by the said court of appeal below; and for the said purpose, the case should have been remanded to the said Court for a fresh adjudication of the appeal, but if, the learned Judges were so minded as to dispose of the appeal themselves they should have decided the case on evidence just like a court of fact after giving proper notice to the parties to the said effect.
